context: security-systems-led · secure perimeter & precast cell fit-out drive the programme

brief.intro: New to this project type? A correctional facility is a secure building complex — precast concrete cells, secure perimeter walls or fencing, dormitory/admin blocks — where the structure itself is comparatively straightforward, but the acceptance criteria are not architectural, they are operational. No wing can be handed over until the full chain of security electronics (CCTV, access control, detention door control, intercom/duress) is integrated behind a single PSIM command platform and proven under a live lockdown/life-safety scenario. Your schedule stands or falls on completing the secure perimeter early, treating precast cell delivery as a manufacturing supply chain rather than generic structure, and protecting real time for the security-systems integration and lockdown test at the end.

scope.desc: Security doors/frames, detention-grade glazing and vandal-resistant finishes.

scope.name: Electrical power
scope.desc: Normal and standby (generator/UPS) distribution to keep security systems live through an outage.

scope.name: HVAC & plumbing
scope.desc: Anti-ligature mechanical ventilation and detention-grade, tamper-resistant plumbing fixtures.

scope.name: Fire & life safety
scope.desc: Fire alarm and suppression, interlocked with the lockdown logic rather than standing alone.

scope.name: Security ELV / detention systems
scope.desc: CCTV, access control, electric detention door control and intercom/duress stations.

scope.name: PSIM integration
scope.desc: The Physical Security Information Management platform that ties every security system into one officer interface.

scope.name: Testing & commissioning
scope.desc: Security-systems integration test culminating in a full lockdown / life-safety scenario test.

glossary.plain: Physical Security Information Management — the software platform an officer uses to see and control every security system from one screen.
electrically operated, centrally released high-security locking for cells and secure corridors.
a two-door secure airlock for vehicles or people — the first door must close before the second opens.
fixtures and hardware designed with no points a person could use to self-harm.
a fixed point letting staff or inmates raise an alarm instantly.
the camera network and the video-management software that records and displays it.
a factory-cast concrete cell unit delivered to site and set in place, rather than built in-situ.
a live drill proving every door, alarm and camera responds correctly together during a security incident.

must_get_right: Complete the secure perimeter early — nothing else on site can be safely worked or occupied without it in place.
Sequence precast cell delivery and erection like a manufacturing supply chain, not generic structure — factory lead time and crane/erection windows drive the frame programme.

The security ELV integration (CCTV + access + door control + PSIM) is the true critical path, not the building shell — protect real time for the full lockdown/life-safety scenario test and expect at least one re-test.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities carry durations in working days; the network is calculated (F9) with no artificial constraints beyond contractual and security-clearance milestones. Total float is kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and precast-erection works run a standard 6-day calendar; once the secure perimeter is closed, access to cellblock zones is restricted to vetted and escorted personnel, which is modelled as a reduced-productivity calendar for those areas; security-ELV and PSIM commissioning runs an extended-hours calendar to protect the integration and lockdown-test window.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs secure perimeter completion → precast cell delivery & erection → security ELV rough-in (CCTV, access, door control) → PSIM integration → full lockdown / life-safety scenario test → handover. The building shell and admin fit-out are not on the critical path once the perimeter is closed and cell modules are erected.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design and security-hardware specifications are frozen and authority approvals obtained per phase gate; the secure perimeter is complete before internal security-clearance zones are worked; a single mobilisation; personnel vetting/clearance for restricted zones is arranged ahead of need. Any change to these invalidates the baseline dates.

sections.heading: Procurement & long-lead items
sections.body: The schedule is driven by specialist security and precast supply chains. The following are tracked as milestones and drive the network:

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Once the secure perimeter closes, all site personnel must be security-vetted and escorted into cellblock zones, which limits daily crew size and access windows; precast erection requires crane windows and clear laydown; security-hardware installers and PSIM integrators are specialist, scarce trades concentrated late in the programme.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: precast module supply-chain slippage, security-hardware/PSIM integration debugging, and lockdown-test re-runs. Schedule contingency is held immediately before the security integration test and again before the full lockdown/life-safety scenario test, rather than spread thinly across the network.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
